cells.tense: You're at the bench while something you've been tending is coming up, and you know it's coming up because of you.
cells.ask: Offer to let one person see what all that tending was for — not the work, the want behind it. Then let their seeing land as what it is: proof it was real.
cells.core:
You've got your hands in something that's still growing, and you're not clenching it. You water, you wait, you let it be a plant instead of a project. Nothing has to pay you back yet, and that's what lets it stay alive.

That quiet tending is already giving you something to steer by — a direction you trust because you made it, not borrowed it. The want underneath it is close to out in the open now. Say that want where one other person can hear it, once, and the completion you've been working toward can be something you release instead of something you grip.
cells.sheetLine: You tend it, you don't clutch it, and you know it's yours.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible hands
cells.place: in the pull toward what you're reaching for

cells.tense: You're watering something that hasn't been planted yet, and you can see it fully grown.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're holding be unshaped for a day — no plan, no picture of where it's headed. Let felt experience, not ahead-of-time vision, decide what comes next.
cells.core:
You can already see it finished. So you're out ahead of it, bracing it against the season it's not in, smoothing a path that doesn't exist yet. The tending is genuine. It just has nowhere to land, so it doubles back and starts bossing the thing it's trying to grow.

What this looks like when it's good is a garden someone tends and then leaves alone — growth without forcing, a hand that doesn't exhaust itself. You get back there by dreaming out of what you've actually lived instead of what you're afraid of next. Fulfillment comes when imagination draws from what happened, not from what you're dreading.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future that hasn't arrived to be tended.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible hands
cells.place: in the pull toward what you're reaching for

cells.tense: You had hold of something you were growing, and you've stopped reaching for it.
cells.ask: Pick the hope you haven't named in a while — the one you're still going for — and tell one person it's still what you want. That hope is the fuel; it does the pulling so you don't have to push.
cells.core:
There was a thing you were tending, and somewhere along the way your hands came off it. The wanting is still there. It's just gone quiet, and quietly has a way of feeling like it's over.

When this is good, it's a garden you keep planting even in a bad year — care that doesn't exhaust because you're not forcing a harvest, just showing up. You don't get back there by pushing effort into the starved spot. You get back there by letting genuine hope pull you, and by trusting development to shine on its own once the work underneath it is done.
cells.sheetLine: You put the growing down, and the pull toward it got quiet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible hands
cells.place: in the pull toward what you're reaching for

cells.tense: You're steering by something, and what's guiding you isn't something you've claimed as chosen.
cells.ask: Say that the direction you're on is yours — out loud, to one person, as the thing you've been choosing while calling it circumstance.
cells.core:
You already know what you want. The choosing is running — every turn you make goes toward it — but you talk about the pull as though it were happening to you. Something decided, and it decided through you, and it hasn't been said.

What this looks like when you're on your own side is care that holds without clutching, growth that isn't forced, a hand steady because it chose to be steady. You get there by letting the want be visible and witnessed instead of carried silently. That's not a defeat. It's what finishing looks like — you let go because the thing is actually done.
cells.sheetLine: You're already steering by it. You just haven't called it yours.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible hands
cells.place: in the pull toward what you're reaching for
